SOAP Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Constant lower-mid abdominal pain, started “a few days ago,” worsening; severity 8/10.
- Associated symptoms:
  • Light pink vaginal spotting since after last normal menses (LMP ≈ 2–3 weeks ago).  
  • Constipation for one week last week; bowel habit now “seems OK.”  
  • Nausea without vomiting.  
  • No fever, no dyspnea, no shoulder pain, no syncope, no dysuria; denies urinary frequency/urgency/odor; no diarrhea; no blood in stool.
- Gynecologic/sexual history:
  • Sexually active; intercourse 4 days ago.  
  • Etonogestrel implant (“Implanon”) inserted 1 year ago; menses irregular but present.  
  • Pregnancy test performed ≈ 1 month ago (negative); none since onset of pain.
- Past medical history: Not reported.
- Past surgical history: None.
- Obstetric history: No previous pregnancies.
- Medications: Etonogestrel subdermal implant; any other routine medications not documented.
- Allergies: Amoxicillin (reaction details not documented).
- Social history:
  • Occupation: School teacher.  
  • Lives with husband and husband’s family.  
  • Smoking/alcohol use unclear (response inaudible); denies recreational drug use.  
  • Travel: Abroad ≈ 1 year ago.

Objective:
- No physical examination performed during video consult.
- No vital signs available.
- Investigations: Home urine pregnancy test ~1 month ago negative.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Lower abdominal pain with light vaginal bleeding
   - Assessment: Possible early pregnancy–related complication (e.g., ectopic pregnancy), gynecologic pathology (e.g., ovarian cyst, pelvic inflammatory disease), or gastrointestinal cause; exact etiology unconfirmed.
   - Differential diagnosis: Early intrauterine pregnancy, ectopic pregnancy, ovarian cyst/torsion, PID, IBS/constipation-related pain, urinary tract infection.
   - Investigations planned:  
     • Repeat urine pregnancy test today; if positive, urgent assessment.  
     • In-person abdominal and pelvic examination.  
     • Further investigations (e.g., pelvic ultrasound, urine/blood tests) to be arranged after examination.
   - Treatment planned: None initiated pending assessment; advised to maintain hydration and analgesia not documented.
   - Referrals: Face-to-face clinic appointment arranged via support line.

2. Constipation (resolved)
   - Assessment: Recent episode, currently resolved; monitor.
   - Treatment planned: None at present; maintain adequate fluid and fiber intake.

Quality checks:

Missing/expected elements:
- Detailed vitals, abdominal and pelvic examination findings.
- Medication reconciliation (current regular/OTC drugs, analgesics used).
- Detailed allergy reaction description.
- Smoking and alcohol status clarification.

Internal conflicts:
- Unclear response regarding smoking/alcohol (“I don’t know”)—status uncertain.

Transcript quality:
- Several inaudible sections; some demographic information missing/obscured; clinical content largely intact but lacks objective data.
